chunks: And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
If you are in a situation in which you find nothing but clay, then there is no harm in performing tayammum with it.

key_terms.الطِّينَ: clay or mud used here as the available substance for tayammum
key_terms.بَأْسَ: harm or objection; here it means there is no problem or prohibition
key_terms.تَتَيَمَّمَ: to perform tayammum, the dry ablution in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.حَالٍ: a circumstance or condition in which the ruling applies

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform tayammum with clay when no other earth is available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning tayammum when ordinary earth is unavailable and only clay is found. It indicates that using clay for tayammum is permitted in a state of necessity, showing the facilitation present in the laws of ritual purity.
